messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: TrafficShiftMonitor detected sudden cross-region routing flips (us-west-2 <-> eu-west-1). Error-rate spike on /v1/generate for customers pinned to eu-west-1. group: routing, severity: P1. auto-page -> pagerduty.

pagerduty: Paging on-call: @oncall-sre. Escalation policy: Cross-region routing faults.

oncall-sre: I’m up. Looking at dashboards now. alex are you able to join?

alex: on it. seeing 5xx rate jump from 0.2% -> 6% in last 3m. latency tail also up for eu-west-1 pinned shards. traces show requests landing in us-west-2 but with eu model pins.

maria: digging into routing control plane. I just checked the routing-policy service: last deploy 1790009000 by infra-ci. There was a rule change to prefer latency-based routing fallback. Rolling it back now for eu region pinning.

jun: can we confirm whether this is DNS or our smart-router policy? I see a matching BGP announcement drift in the cloud provider console for us-west-2.

samira: Customer reports coming in: big-ticket SaaS customer in EU seeing failed completions and high latency. Ticket #9876. Notified CSE.

alex: quick check: correlate request logs by X-Region header. Example curl for logs: 
```
curl -s "https://logs.internal/api/search?q=service:router AND request.path:/v1/generate AND region:eu-west-1" | jq '.hits | length'
```

maria: rollback started: reverting latency-fallback rule. New config diff: removed fallback_to_low_latency for policy eu-pin. Pushing now.

incident-bot: config-change detected: routing-policy-service reverted by maria at 1790012503.

jun: DNS checks: eu-west-1 edge still resolving to us-west-2 IPs intermittently. TTL is 60s. I'm forcing a negative cache flush and lowering TTL to 10s for affected records. Commands run against our provider: 
```
# provider console CLI
provider dns update-record --zone redwood.ai --name api.eu --value 3.10.22.45 --ttl 10
```

alex: I’m temporarily enabling strict-region-pin on the proxy for eu-west-1 pinned shards to bypass runtime routing decisions. Command: 
```
redwoodctl proxy set-policy --region eu-west-1 --strict-pin=true --reason "mitigate cross-region misroutes"
```

katie: FYI, I toggled the canary rollback in the control plane — traffic shifted back to eu-west-1 within 30s. Error rate dropping to ~0.8% now.

samira: Customer-facing update drafted and sent to CSE: "We identified a cross-region routing regression, mitigations in place, some customers may have seen increased latency and failures between 12:14-12:36 UTC. Teams are monitoring, will update in 30m."

oncall-sre: Good. Please also ask CSE to apply temporary retry guidance for customers with strict pinning, suggested header X-Retry-After: 2s.

jun: Cloud provider confirmed an internal route flap in their backbone between us-west-2 and eu-west-1 that caused our latency-based fallback to prefer the wrong POP for some sessions. They claim partial resolution at 1790013000.

maria: Post-rollback, routing-policy-service metrics show stable region affinity. No new deploys planned. I've created a feature-flag to gate latency-fallback in the short term: flag id ff-1827.

alex: On-call action items so far: strict-pin enabled, routing rollback, lowered DNS TTL, proxy policy set, CSE notified. Observability: continue to watch error rate and p50/p95.

incident-bot: NOTE: Active pages escalated: none pending. Scheduled follow-up reminder in 45m.

katie: I’m taking over 1hr handoff in 30m. alex, can you summarize anything to add?

alex: Summary for handoff: root cause appears to be a combination of provider backbone route flap + our latency-fallback policy which briefly overrode explicit region pinning. Immediate mitigations removed the fallback, enforced strict-pin, and lowered DNS TTL to reduce cached misroutes. Customer impact window ~1790012440-1790013000 (approx 9m). Current status: stabilizing, error-rate ~0.4%, no active escalations. Logs and diffs: /internal/incidents/1790012345/artifacts.

samira: Adding open action: investigate adding a circuit-breaker in routing-policy when cross-region shifts exceed threshold. Ticket created INFRA-3212.

jun: Also request a postmortem with the network provider to get timeline of their flap. I’ll open support loop.

oncall-sre: Handing off to katie. katie, you have the next watch. If we see error-rate >1% or customer reports spike, page everyone.

katie: Acknowledged. Handoff notes saved. Will run a 15m check and post update.

alex: small note: we should consider adding a pre-flight check in routing CI that simulates provider route flaps and verifies pinning precedence. Filing RFC next week.

incident-bot: Reminder: incident follow-up meeting scheduled in 2h. Please include routing, infra, and SRE representatives.

katie: Update at 1790015600: stable. p95 latency back to baseline, error-rate <0.5%. Closing on-call watch; follow-up doc to be posted by alex.

samira: Thanks everyone. Will keep ticket updated and coordinate customer postmortem comms. :thumbsup:
